description: main is kept strictly linear — a ruleset on main with 'require linear history' + the logic-test/domain-audit/build checks turns the invariant from a convention into a gate (see CONTRIBUTING.md). That ruleset ALSO carried 'require signed commits' and no longer does: this bot authenticates with a PAT, and GitHub signs a bot's API commits only for a GitHub App — measured, not assumed (run 30169946598 committed through the API path with a PAT and produced `verified: false, unsigned`), so every PR opened here was blocked with green checks and zero required approvals. Automerge MUST squash either way: a squash merge stays linear AND is signed by GitHub's web-flow key, whereas a merge commit would break linearity and force a from-root re-linearize (git rebase --root + force-push) that rewrites every SHA — orphaning and auto-closing every open PR. platformAutomerge is off so Renovate self-merges once CI is green, instead of leaving green PRs open where the next force-push would close them.

packageRules.description: Never auto-merge a tracked firmware dependency. A green build proves the firmware compiles — it does NOT prove the X10A decode path still matches a real heat pump, that WiFi/MQTT behaviour survives an ESP-IDF bump, or that the browser installer still flashes (esp-web-tools, which the build never exercises). A human reviews and merges these manually. GitHub Action digest bumps are unaffected and keep auto-merging.
Remind to re-check the ESP-IDF API surface on a major bump.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **On a major ESP-IDF bump — check the migration guide.** Mbed TLS and component moves (cJSON is already a managed dep) plus `esp-mqtt`/`esp_https_ota` TLS can change. Confirm the CI `build` job is green for the esp32s3 target.
